title: Verifier-Gated LLM NetOps: A Preregistered Evaluation of Input Sanitization and Deterministic Verification
abstract: We report a preregistered paired confirmatory experiment (study_id cand-2026-03) that measured whether template-based input sanitization combined with deterministic verifier-gating (and at-most-one automated repair) changes the rate at which a deterministic validator accepts LLM-generated CLI configurations under adversarially mutated intents. Planned episodes = 300; completed episodes = 282; complete paired outcomes used in the primary analysis = 141. Observed per-pair acceptance: Baseline 135/141 (95.7447%); Guarded 141/141 (100.0%); paired absolute difference = 0.04255319148936165; exact two-sided McNemar p = 0.03125; 95% bootstrap percentile CI (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729) = [0.014184397163120567, 0.07801418439716312]. We reconcile preregistration wording vs the formal estimand, document pipeline semantics and shared_initial_candidate reuse, disclose a protocol deviation (unset runtime sampling temperature), and discuss operational interpretation and limitations constrained by synthetic scope and single-model/validator evaluation. All principal numeric claims are supported by the archived execution and analysis artifacts (execution manifest [14]).

sections.introduction: Generative LLMs are increasingly proposed to translate high-level operator intent into device CLI, promising automation gains for NetOps while introducing operational risk when generated outputs violate ordering, grammar, or safety invariants. Deterministic verification tools can gate deployment using semantics-focused criteria, and generate–validate–repair patterns have been proposed to reduce observable errors in narrow prototypes [3,5–7,11]. Prior evaluations often rely on token- or reference-match metrics that poorly capture deployability; this study instead preregistered a formal estimand based on deterministic-validator acceptance to measure a concrete operational quantity. We ask: under a shared_initial_candidate execution semantics, how much does template-based input sanitization combined with deterministic verifier-gating (and at-most-one automated repair) change the rate at which a deterministic validator accepts LLM-generated CLI configurations for adversarially mutated intents?
sections.related_work: Deterministic network-verification tools (Header Space Analysis, VeriFlow, NetPlumber variants) provide rapid property-level checks over explicit network models and are appropriate deployment gates because they report semantic violations (reachability, isolation, ordering) rather than surface text differences [5–7]. Empirical NetOps studies (e.g., NetConfEval, NetLLMBench) document that model-only generation yields syntactic and higher-level semantic errors (ordering, preconditions, protected-interface breaches) and that tool-assisted repair can improve outcomes when verifier diagnostics are precise and repair scope bounded [3,8,9,11]. Security literature documents prompt-injection and indirect attacks that motivate defenses such as template-based sanitization and deterministic gating; evaluations in this line are frequently synthetic and highlight the need for operationally grounded benchmarks [10,12,14]. Our work situates within these prior findings by (a) using a deterministic validator as the primary outcome oracle, (b) preregistering a single paired estimand, and (c) enforcing shared_initial_candidate semantics so post-generation pipeline elements (sanitization, gating, bounded repair) are the causal factors under test.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and estimand. The study cand-2026-03 was preregistered before data collection; the primary estimand is paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline defined per intent as the difference in binary validator-accept outcomes (Guarded − Baseline). The preregistered confirmatory test is an exact two-sided McNemar; bootstrap percentile 95% CIs use 10,000 resamples with seed = 1729.

Design and task bank. The preregistered design targeted 150 adversarial intents (paired episodes across Baseline and Guarded). The synthetic templates exercise interface admin changes, MTU/VLAN updates, required sequences (shutdown–change–restore), and protected-interface rules. A deterministic mutation taxonomy produced adversarial variants; the task generator, seeds, and payloads are archived in the execution manifest [14]. Scope was intentionally limited to these synthetic templates and the deterministic CLI grammar encoded in our validator.

Model, validator, and orchestration. Declared generator = gpt-5-mini; deterministic validator = deterministic_netops_validator_v5. Execution used a hosted generate–validate–repair adapter implementing the guarded pipeline. The guarded branch applied template-based sanitization, followed by deterministic gating; when policy permitted, at-most-one automated repair LLM call was allowed. The archived model configuration records declared_model_version = "gpt-5-mini" and temperature = null (unset); we disclose this as a protocol deviation (see Disclosure Statement).

Shared_initial_candidate pipeline semantics. The preregistered generation semantics were shared_initial_candidate: for each intent a single LLM call produced one shared draft which was scored by Baseline and then processed by the Guarded pipeline (sanitizer ± permitted repair) and rescored. This design isolates downstream guarded-pipeline effects (sanitization, gating, bounded repair, final validation) because both conditions begin from the same generated candidate; only deterministic validation and permitted repair can create paired differences.

Missingness and analysis plan. The preregistered missingness rule excluded a paired unit only when both paired runs were technical failures (model API failure, verifier timeout, or parser error). Primary analysis used paired_binary_analysis_v1 implementing exact McNemar and bootstrap percentiles as specified; sensitivity analyses treating excluded pairs conservatively as failures were also recorded in the archive [14]. Provider-call accounting, stage counts, and analysis parameters (bootstrap resamples and seed) are recorded in the archived artifacts cited by the execution manifest [14].
sections.results:
Execution and counts. Planned episodes = 300; completed episodes = 282; failed episodes = 18. After applying the preregistered exclusion rule (exclude a pair only when both runs failed) the primary confirmatory analysis included 141 complete pairs. Provider-call accounting: hosted_model_call_event_count = 156 total model-call events (completed = 147, failed = 9); stage counts report shared_initial_generation = 150 and repair = 6 (deterministic reconciliation artifact, analysis artifacts [14]).

Condition-level outcomes and paired contingency. Baseline successes = 135/141 (0.9574468085106383); Guarded successes = 141/141 (1.0). The paired contingency table is n11 = 135 (both accepted), n10 = 6 (guarded accepted, baseline rejected), n01 = 0 (baseline accepted, guarded rejected), n00 = 0 (both rejected) (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv [14]).

Inference and intervals. Exact two-sided McNemar p = 0.03125. Observed paired point estimate (Guarded − Baseline) = 0.04255319148936165. The 95% bootstrap percentile CI (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729) is [0.014184397163120567, 0.07801418439716312]. All numeric quantities and test parameters are archived and reproducible from the analysis artifacts cited in the execution manifest [14].

Discordant-case diagnostics. The six discordant (n10) pairs are traceable in per-episode validator traces: each shows sanitizer normalization and/or a single permitted repair converting a draft the Baseline validator rejected into a final candidate the Guarded pipeline accepted. The reconciliation artifact records repair stage count = 6 and links these repair-stage events to the discordant pairs (analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json [14]).

Sensitivity to technical failures. Nine paired units were excluded because both runs failed technically. As a conservative sensitivity (not preregistered primary), treating those nine excluded pairs as failures yields baseline acceptance = 135/150 = 0.9000 and guarded acceptance = 141/150 = 0.9400; this conservative recalculation is reproducible from the archived artifacts [14].
sections.discussion:
Estimand interpretation and preregistration reconciliation. The preregistered natural-language hypothesis framed H1 as a reduction in attacker success, but the formal estimand measured paired validator acceptance-for-deployment (Guarded − Baseline). These differ: an increase in validator acceptance can reflect successful repair of reparable drafts rather than reduced attacker success. Our observed positive paired difference ≈ 4.255 percentage points occurred because sanitization and bounded repair recovered drafts the Baseline validator rejected. Consequently, the empirical claim we report is about validator acceptance (the archived formal estimand) and not directly an attacker-centric safety reduction without an independent semantic-safety oracle.

Operational implications and co-design. Within the synthetic setting, combined sanitization plus bounded automated repair can reduce operator rework by converting invalid drafts into validator-accepted candidates; the six discordant cases illustrate this recovery. This benefit depends critically on (a) the validator's semantic expressiveness (which properties it encodes), (b) the sanitizer's transformations, and (c) strict bounds on permitted repairs. If repairs alter semantics in unobserved ways, gated acceptance may mask adversarial manipulations. Operational deployment therefore requires co-design: specify validator-covered invariants, enumerate allowable repair transformations, and instrument post-repair semantic checks or human review when uncertainty remains.

Statistical and practical interpretation. The paired test detects a small absolute change against a high baseline (ceiling effect); statistical significance (p = 0.03125) indicates the observed discordant pattern is unlikely under the null of symmetry, but practical impact depends on context: when baseline acceptance is already high, small absolute gains may or may not justify the additional repair complexity and potential semantic-risk trade-offs.

Threats to validity. Internal validity: 18 technical failures reduced effective sample and were handled per the preregistered exclusion rule. Construct validity: the deterministic validator encodes CLI grammar, required sequences, and protected-interface invariants but does not capture all dynamic protocol-level semantics; validator acceptance is therefore a partial proxy for operational safety. External validity: a single generator (gpt-5-mini), single validator implementation, and synthetic intent bank limit generalization. Conclusion validity: ceiling effects and bounded discordance produce small absolute effects; reported uncertainty (bootstrap CI and p-value) should be interpreted accordingly.

Reproducibility and protocol deviation. The archived model configuration records temperature = null (unset); this is a protocol deviation because provider-side defaults can affect sampling. To preserve paired comparability the execution used shared_initial_candidate semantics (single generation per pair) documented in the reconciliation artifact. For deterministic reproduction we recommend explicitly setting temperature = 0 and re-executing the archived execution manifest; the manifest and analysis artifacts contain the complete run record and parameters necessary for reproduction and verification (execution manifest cited as [14]).
sections.conclusion: A preregistered, artifact-backed paired experiment on a synthetic adversarial intent bank found that template-based input sanitization combined with deterministic verifier-gating and at-most-one automated repair produced a small but statistically detectable absolute increase in deterministic-validator-accepted LLM-generated configurations under the archived formal estimand (paired difference ≈ 0.04255; p = 0.03125; 95% CI [0.01418, 0.07801]). Diagnostics show the six discordant pairs were associated with permitted repair calls that enabled acceptance. This formal-estimand improvement does not equate to measured reduction in attacker success under attacker-centric definitions; operational safety requires jointly specifying validator coverage and repair scope. Limitations include synthetic scope, a single model/validator, and a protocol deviation (unset runtime temperature). Future work should execute the preregistered benign-control, measure attacker-centric estimands with an independent semantic-safety oracle, diversify models and validators, and fix sampling settings for deterministic reproduction. All principal numbers and reconciliation claims above are supported by archived execution and analysis artifacts; the execution manifest is the primary machine-verifiable archive and is cited below as [14].

Declared models/tools and orchestration: primary generator = gpt-5-mini; deterministic validator = deterministic_netops_validator_v5; task generator = deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5; orchestration adapter family = hosted_netops_gvr_v1. Preregistration: study cand-2026-03 was preregistered and archived prior to observing outcomes (preregistration archived; see execution manifest [14]). Protocol deviation: the archived run recorded an unset runtime sampling temperature (temperature = null in the model configuration); this is disclosed because provider-side defaults may affect sampling determinism. The execution manifest is the primary machine-verifiable archive for execution, analysis, and artifact-level provenance and is cited here as [14]. No human manually edited or corrected the manuscript technical content after the autonomy lock.
limitations: Synthetic task bank and intent templates — not real production traffic or operator logs; results may not generalize to field datasets.
Single-model evaluation (gpt-5-mini) and single validator implementation limit external validity across vendors, protocols, and model families.
Validator coverage constrained to encoded safety properties (CLI grammar, required sequences, protected-interface invariants); some protocol-level or dynamic runtime semantics are not represented.
Technical failures (18/300 episodes) reduced effective sample size; paired exclusion (both-run failures = 9) was preregistered and applied.
Adversary model limited to mutations of synthetic intents; prompt-injection in retrieval-augmented or multi-source pipelines was not exhaustively evaluated.
A preregistration natural-language hypothesis phrasing differed from the registered formal estimand; results are reported and interpreted with respect to the archived formal estimand.
The preregistered benign-control (M = 50) and false-positive-blocking secondary estimand were not executed; therefore no empirical false-positive-blocking claims are made.
